answer_summary: The stone is aluminium mellitate hexadecahydrate, Al2[C6(COO)6].16H2O (Al2C12O12.16H2O), and compound H is Al2O3.
assumptions: Atomic weights are the exact values printed on supplied PDF page G1-5.
The A4 and A5 qualitative analyses identify Al(III) and mellitate(6-) as the salt ions; charge neutrality fixes Al2[mellitate].
The approximately 100-200 C mass loss is hydrate water, so the dry-to-initial mass ratio is the anhydrous-to-hydrated molar-mass ratio.
Complete heating in open air converts the mellitate carbon and hydrogen to volatile CO2 and H2O, leaving stable aluminium oxide as the nonvolatile product.
